dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL CGI program using embedded SQL (likely MySQL/MariaDB via ESQL preprocessor), part of the 'openjensen' educational system. Uses *> comment style and GOBACK, typical of GnuCOBOL. Targets a web CGI context calling dynamic libraries like 'wui-print-header', 'wui-start-html'.
evidence: EXEC SQL CONNECT :wc-username IDENTIFIED BY :wc-passwd USING :wc-database

purpose.domain_detail: Student grade/course management system ('betyg' is Swedish for grade, 'elev' is student). Part of a school/educational administration web application called 'openjensen'.
purpose.summary: A CGI COBOL program that fetches a list of courses and grades for a specific student (identified by user_id and program_id) from SQL tables tbl_course and tbl_grade. It writes the results as comma-separated records to a text file (betyg-elev.txt) for consumption by a PHP front-end. Courses without grades are also listed with a placeholder value.

notable_features: EXEC SQL embedded SQL with cursor declarations (cursgrade, cursprog)
EXEC SQL CONNECT with IDENTIFIED BY / USING syntax (MySQL-style)
CGI web integration via dynamic library calls (wui-print-header, wui-start-html, wui-end-html)
POST parameter parsing via 'get-post-value' and 'write-post-string' calls
Output written to flat file as CSV for PHP consumption
OCCURS table for tracking completed course IDs
verdict.notes: The program has two 01-level items both named 'wr-rec-vars' in the WORKING-STORAGE section which would be a compile error in strict COBOL; this may be a copy-paste artifact or the second is intended to shadow/replace the first. The SQL CONNECT syntax (IDENTIFIED BY ... USING) is MySQL-style. The file is part of a Swedish educational web application. One line exceeds 72 columns. Overall structure is well-organized and production-like despite the duplicate record name issue.
